bug_semantics: The HTML writer passed an attacker-controlled cell value through a custom number format and escaped the result only when the formatted string exactly equalled the original value. For an unquoted @ text placeholder plus any literal text, such as '. @' or '@ ', Formatter substituted the raw cell value and returned early without invoking the HTML writer's escaping callback; the added literal made the formatted value unequal to the original, so Writer/Html.php also skipped htmlspecialchars(). An uploaded spreadsheet could therefore emit a raw script-capable tag into generated HTML and cause stored XSS when that HTML was viewed.
flaw_origin: The completing write is edc003ad164521d10d96ac9f2f670b543511b806, which first made Formatter::toFormattedString substitute a raw string cell into an unquoted @ format mask and return before the writer callback. Direct parent ad0b68c7cbd414c8de9e06c0447f2d20bf8a8d02 still returned non-numeric values unchanged, so Writer/Html.php's pre-existing `$cellData === $origData` htmlspecialchars still ran. PR #1464 member 62da380674d68bd6bc432c88146fd965246d9085 (later squash-landed as 97a80f383c1487e18c70a097b6ba2352dfd764cf) introduced that equality guard but did not yet apply @ formats to strings; it is a latent sink, not the BIC for this advisory.

evidence: CVE.org record CVE-2026-40296 is PUBLISHED and describes stored XSS caused by Writer/Html skipping escaping when custom @ number formats make the formatted value differ; it lists affected ranges through 1.30.3, 2.1.15, 2.4.4, 3.10.4, and 5.6.0 and fixes 1.30.4, 2.1.16, 2.4.5, 3.10.5, and 5.7.0.

GitHub PR #1464 /commits exposes the pre-squash member history. git diff 1861412d608f5e66ed0155632b5b93d9ba5c94bc..62da380674d68bd6bc432c88146fd965246d9085 -- src/PhpSpreadsheet/Writer/Html.php shows unconditional '$cellData = htmlspecialchars($cellData)' removed and the equality-guarded escape added around the NumberFormat::toFormattedString result.

Direct parent-tree verification: 1861412d608f5e66ed0155632b5b93d9ba5c94bc:src/PhpSpreadsheet/Writer/Html.php lines 1247-1260 unconditionally call htmlspecialchars() after either formatted-value path; the vulnerable equality guard is absent.

reasoning: The vulnerability is real and published, and the release boundaries agree with the repository topology. The unsafe lifecycle begins when PR #1464 member 62da380674d68bd6bc432c88146fd965246d9085 replaces the parent's unconditional post-format escaping with equality-conditional escaping. The custom unquoted-@ formatter path can preserve attacker HTML, alter the surrounding string so equality fails, and bypass the callback, closing the source-to-sink mechanism. Although GitHub squash-landed the PR as 97a80f383c1487e18c70a097b6ba2352dfd764cf, the publicly reconstructable member is the smaller causal BIC and its direct parent proves absence. Fix f1eb4e6980d537ec85fc20be5950f9ad65d47ffd routes the previously early-returning unquoted-@ path through the callback that HTML writer uses to escape PCDATA; branch-equivalent fixes align with every advisory patched boundary. The BIC commit object has ordinary human author/committer identity and no AI marker, so the proper closed verdict is NOT_AI regardless of unrelated AI-marked commits elsewhere in the repository.
